title: 2026 Iowa gubernatorial election
description: Iowa’s 2026 gubernatorial election will choose the state’s next governor after incumbent Kim Reynolds declined to seek re-election. The race features Democratic state Auditor Rob Sand and a Republican primary field that includes U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra, state Rep. Eddie Andrews, former state Rep. Brad Sherman, former state agency director Adam Steen, and businessman-farmer Zach Lahn. Early contrasts center on fundraising, endorsements, and policy emphasis, including Sand’s election-reform agenda, Feenstra’s Washington ties and fundraising edge, and the GOP field’s competing appeals to grassroots conservatives and anti-establishment voters.

candidates.name: Rob Sand
candidates.summary: Rob Sand is Iowa’s state auditor and the Democratic candidate for governor in 2026. In April 2026, he unveiled an election-reform-focused policy agenda that includes term limits, age and cognitive tests for elected officials, and a proposal to replace Iowa’s current two-party primary system with a top-four, ranked-style general election format.

Healthcare.stance: Sand says Iowa’s privatized Medicaid system is harming access and payment for care, and he has called for better support for telehealth, more rural health care infrastructure, and expanded loan forgiveness to keep doctors in Iowa.

Economy.stance: Sand’s campaign focuses on lowering costs, improving government efficiency, and growing the economy. He argues Iowa needs a new direction and says better oversight can reduce waste and make the state more attractive to workers and families.

reviews.summary: This profile is a well-constructed and balanced overview of the 2026 Iowa gubernatorial race, with accurate representations of candidates' positions drawn from credible sources like Ballotpedia, campaign websites, and reputable news outlets such as the Des Moines Register and KCCI. The career histories for Rob Sand are thoroughly documented with specific timelines and sources, while issue stances are clearly linked to high-confidence evidence, demonstrating strong attention to neutrality and completeness in areas like healthcare and education.

forecast.rationale: No candidate-level polling is available in the provided race data, and no polls have been published after 2026-04-01 in the available sources, so this forecast is highly uncertain. Iowa has leaned Republican in recent statewide elections, which gives the GOP a modest baseline advantage even in an open-seat race. However, the lack of a settled Republican nominee and the presence of Democratic statewide officeholder Rob Sand, who appears to be a credible and established candidate, keep the race competitive rather than clearly favoring either party.
